name: Topic 32: Electrolytes and hydration during exercise
defaultTargetFormula: Daily target = Topic 30 formula (base + weight_adjust + min(workout_minutes*8, 1000) + heat_add), clamp 1500-4500 ml. Before: 300-500 ml in the 2 h before (about 5-7 ml/kg, est.; ACSM 2007 about 500 ml, Academy/DC/ACSM 2016 5-10 ml/kg secondary). During: sip 150-250 ml every 15-20 min on workouts over 30 min, drink to thirst, max 750 ml/h (est.). Electrolyte tip if workout >= 60 min AND (hot_weather OR salty_sweat OR workout >= 90 min); sodium plus carbohydrate if >= 120 min. After: 1.2-1.5 x kg lost x 1000 ml over 4-6 h (Sports Dietitians Australia 125-150%; ACSM 1.5 L/kg secondary), extra fluid cap 3000 ml/day (est.). ICMR-NIN 2020 exercise-fluid values Not found.

drinks.name: Plain water
drinks.notes: Enough for sessions under about 60 min

drinks.name: Nimbu-namak-shakkar pani (homemade)
drinks.notes: About 1/2 tsp salt per litre (about 1,180 mg sodium per litre, est.) plus light sugar; for 60 min or more; not for doctor-flag users

drinks.name: Tender coconut water
drinks.notes: Potassium about 165-310 mg per 100 g, sodium low and variable (secondary, unverified); some bloating

drinks.name: Chaas (buttermilk, salted)
drinks.notes: Sodium about 68-105 mg per 100 g unsalted in non-Indian databases (secondary); count added salt (Topic 18)

drinks.name: Sports drink
drinks.notes: About 6 g carbohydrate and 45-49 mg sodium per 100 ml (retail listings, secondary); for over 60 min

drinks.name: WHO-formula ORS
drinks.notes: 75 mmol/L sodium, 75 mmol/L glucose, 245 mOsm/L; for illness or heat illness, not daily

drinks.name: Chai or coffee
drinks.notes: est.; up to about 450 mg caffeine per day showed no extra dehydration in regular users; sugar

drinks.name: Energy drink
drinks.notes: est.; product policy; caffeine and sugar

drinks.name: Soft drink
drinks.notes: est.; product policy; sugar and caffeine

drinksTable.notes: About 1/2 tsp salt per litre (about 1,180 mg sodium per litre, est.), light sugar; for 60 min or more, not for BP or kidney users

drinksTable.drink: Plain nimbu pani with sugar only
drinksTable.notes: Sugar, no sodium; keep for short sessions or add a pinch of salt
Potassium about 165-310 mg per 100 g, sodium low (2-105 mg per 100 g, secondary); some bloating; short sessions or after workout
Sodium about 68-105 mg per 100 g unsalted (non-Indian databases, secondary) plus added salt; protein; best after workout with a meal
About 6 g carbohydrate and 45-49 mg sodium per 100 ml (secondary); useful over 60 min

drinksTable.drink: Zero-sugar electrolyte drink or tablet in water
drinksTable.notes: Sodium varies by product; check label; no carbohydrate for long sessions
75 mmol/L sodium (about 1,725 mg per litre, calc.); illness or heat illness; not an everyday gym drink
Caffeine about 30-120 mg per cup (secondary); sugar; fine before a workout for regular drinkers
Protein, sodium and potassium; sugar if sweetened
High caffeine and sugar; not for hydration
Sugar, caffeine, fizz; poor choice during exercise

reminderRules.rule: During a logged workout over 30 min, prompt a 150-250 ml sip at most every 20 min; stop prompting when the user says not thirsty after the first 30 min
reminderRules.source: FitPlate design (est.); EAH consensus 2015 drink to thirst; ACSM 2007 individualised plans

reminderRules.rule: Never prompt more than 750 ml per hour; after 2 h show 'drink to thirst'
reminderRules.source: FitPlate design (est.); hyponatraemia caution, EAH consensus 2015

reminderRules.rule: One after-session prompt 30 min after workout end showing 1.2-1.5 x kg lost x 1,000 ml over 4-6 h
reminderRules.source: Sports Dietitians Australia 125-150% (via snippet); ACSM 1.5 L/kg (secondary)

reminderRules.rule: If post-session weight is 0.5 kg or more above pre-session weight, show 'stop adding fluid'
reminderRules.source: FitPlate design (est.); EAH consensus (weight gain suggests overdrinking)

reminderRules.rule: Doctor-flag users (kidney, heart, liver, BP medicines, diuretics, fluid or salt limit): no exercise-fluid or electrolyte prompts; show 'Follow your doctor's fluid and salt advice'
reminderRules.source: FitPlate safety design; Topic 18 and Topic 30 convention

warnings: Do not drink more than you sweat; over-drinking in long events can cause low blood sodium; drink to thirst.
Electrolyte drinks and added salt are not for users with kidney, heart or liver disease, salt or fluid limits, BP medicines or diuretics unless their doctor says so.
ORS is for illness or heat illness, not for daily gym use.
ICMR-NIN 2020 exercise-fluid values Not found; app logic uses ACSM, NATA, EAH consensus and Sports Dietitians Australia figures, several via secondary summaries (secondary, unverified).
Sweat sodium varies about 10-100 mmol/L between people; no India-specific sweat study was found.
